title: Debenture by-laws approved for Kitchener and Region
subtitle: Special meeting also authorized an All Councils session, held a closed session on labour and land lease matters, and noted International Day of Persons with Disabilities.
overview: Regional Council met in a short special meeting to approve the borrowing needed for capital works. Three by-laws authorized instalment debentures: $35,657,000 for the City of Kitchener, $38,343,000 for the Region, and a combined issue of $74,000,000 that brings the two together. Staff's debenture issue report, dated December 5, 2024, was received for information.
Council also authorized taking part in an All Councils meeting on December 6, 2024 at 2:00 p.m. at Centre in the Square {{vote:m2}}.

Council then moved into a closed session of its standing committees. The minutes list subjects including employee negotiations, labour relations involving the Ontario Municipal Employee Retirement System, a proposed land lease in Cambridge, and legal advice. No decisions from that session are reported in the minutes. The Chair also marked the International Day of Persons with Disabilities. The meeting adjourned at 9:07 a.m.

decisions.detail: Council authorized borrowing through ten-year instalment debentures of $35,657,000 for City of Kitchener capital works.
Council authorized borrowing of $38,343,000 for Regional capital works, made up of $14,343,000 in ten-year and $24,000,000 in twenty-year instalment debentures.

Council approved one series of instalment debentures totalling $74,000,000, made up of $50,000,000 in ten-year and $24,000,000 in twenty-year debentures, covering the amounts in by-laws 24-045 and 24-046.
Council authorized taking part in an All Councils meeting on December 6, 2024 at 2:00 p.m. at Centre in the Square.

debate: The transcript records no substantive debate. The Chair asked whether anyone had questions on the debenture report, and none were raised.
Members voted on each motion without discussion, with some confusion over the electronic voting system. One person said they were in closed session and could not see the vote.
